item.title: By: Leah

item.description: Ahh, yes, the whole preconception concept. I much like that correlation essay, and it really is a good piece of 'advice' if you can let your "preconceptions slowly give way to cautious contemplation and lingering contentment."

item.title: By: carl
item.dc:creator: carl
item.description:
<blockquote>One thing you didn’t mention is the culture in which you learn your language and how it affects the way you communicate with one person to the other.</blockquote>
Oh absolutely! And not only how we communicate with each other but internally with ourselves. I've commented quite a lot on that angle previously. One of the make purposes of the <a href="https://centertao.local/essays/correlations/" rel="nofollow">correlations</a> was to deconstruct that internal conversation, and see life anew (i.e., <a href="https://centertao.local/tao-te-ching/dc-lau/#chapter-28" rel="nofollow">again return to being a babe...return to being the uncarved block</a>). Alas, correlations don't seem to work for people as well as I had imagined.

item.title: By: Leah
item.dc:creator: Leah
item.description:
So much can be analyzed about the way humans think down to almost an animal-like nature. (But that's what we are- animals.)
One thing you didn't mention is the culture in which you learn your language and how it affects the way you communicate with one person to the other.
Your core beliefs are given to you by your religion. So if you are Christian, if somebody were to tell you, "There is no God," then your immediate response would be anger and self-defense. But were you Atheist, you would have more-or-less agreed.
Those who are raised in a Christian settings will (most likely) steer clear of swearing, but those who weren't raised around a religion probably could care less.
